segments.title: Chương 100: 【Con đường hoang dã vãi】
segments.content:
Chapter 103: His Methods Are So Damn Wild

Under the Banyan Tree were three horse-drawn carriages, namely: Li Xunhuan, Ning Caishen, and Xing Yusen.

If you added Anni Baobei, they would be known as the Four Great Writers.

Of course, many others wrote there. Han Han and Guo Xiaosi had also joined. There were also Cai Jun, Jin Hezai, Murong Xuecun, Bu Feiyan, Rao Xueman, and so on.

Everyone is probably very familiar with Ning Caishen.

Xing Yusen has already switched careers to become a screenwriter, mainly writing sitcoms like "Idler Ma Dajie," "A Family in the Northeast," "Home with Kids," and so on.

Li Xunhuan was the most unique one. Besides being a writer, he also held the position of editor-in-chief at Rongshu Xia. Zhu Weilian had poached him from Beijing, offering him a monthly salary of over ten thousand yuan back in 1999, plus a rented villa for him in Shanghai.

After Rongshu Xia was acquired by Bertelsmann, Zhu Weilian jumped ship to Shanda to be a senior manager. Li Xunhuan, on the other hand, cashed out his shares and started his own book publishing business.

This man's methods were a bit wild, different from traditional publishing houses.

What does "wild" mean?

Li Xunhuan walked into the coffee shop, saw his competitor hadn't left yet, and came out swinging with his very first sentence: "A 15% royalty, plus a tiered-share."

"What did you say?" Shi Xiang shot to his feet.

Chen Guiliang actually wanted to ask the same four words.

I haven't even started my move yet, and you're already offering terms that exceed the industry standard? What have I done to deserve this!

Li Xunhuan repeated himself: "A 15% royalty, plus a tiered-share."

"You're insane! You're just making a mess, you'll disrupt the publishing market!" Shi Xiang's composure had shattered.

The customers in the coffee shop all looked over. Shi Xiang's voice had been a bit loud just now.

Li Xunhuan smiled without a word.

Shi Xiang ignored the gazes of the surrounding customers and said to Chen Guiliang in a low voice, "This person just got into publishing. His company hasn't been open long, and he hasn't successfully launched a single book. Even if he offered you a 50% royalty, your book wouldn't sell more than a few copies."

Chen Guiliang said nothing, turning his head to look at Li Xunhuan.

Li Xunhuan said, "Starting from 1999, I was involved in every book that Rongshu Xia arranged for publication. I have sufficient channel resources on hand, I'm just short of a bestseller that can take off. Moreover, although my company is newly opened, I'm not short on operational funds. I used to have shares in Rongshu Xia, and I cashed out a large sum of money when Bertelsmann acquired it."

Chen Guiliang still didn't speak, turning his head to look at Shi Xiang.

Shi Xiang said, "Guo Xiaosi is on very good terms with him. He even asked this person for help when starting his company and magazine. But why didn't he let him publish his new book? It's because he's unreliable!"

Chen Guiliang smiled and turned his head to look at Li Xunhuan again.

Li Xunhuan explained, "Three reasons. First, Guo Xiaosi's book is a collection of pictures and text, which can only be sold to loyal fans. It's destined not to sell too well. So I didn't offer a very high royalty, nor did I need to use it to curry favor, as I'd already discussed other collaborations with him. Second, Guo Xiaosi's personality is overly cautious, which is why he chose a more conservative, traditional publishing house. Third, Guo Xiaosi was unwilling to bow his head to Zhuang Yu, so he rejected my operational plan."

The coffee arrived. Li Xunhuan picked up a spoon and said to Chen Guiliang, "Your book is different. I have very high hopes for it."

Chen Guiliang's smile widened as he once again turned his head to look at Shi Xiang.

Shi Xiang stuck to his previous argument: "His company is just a slapdash operation. A smart person wouldn't trust him. Guo Xiaosi is a smart person, so no matter how good their relationship is, he wouldn't let him publish his book."

Chen Guiliang finally spoke: "Editor Shi, is there any room to raise your royalty offer?"

Raise it, my ass!

Shi Xiang's authority was capped at 10%. To go any higher, he'd have to ask his superiors. And his boss, at the very most, could raise it to 12% for Chen Guiliang.

Across the entire country, no legitimate publishing house would likely offer a higher price. Chunfeng Literature and Art was already considered very open-minded, otherwise it wouldn't have earned its title as the "vanguard" of youth literature.

Shi Xiang usually mocked other publishing houses for being too conservative.

But in front of Li Xunhuan, Shi Xiang had also become the conservative one.

His methods were so damn wild.

What was the highest price Li Xunhuan had offered Han Han? A 20% royalty! Later, they simply became partners, and after deducting costs, Han Han could take 50% of the profits.

Shi Xiang couldn't answer Chen Guiliang's question. Instead, he challenged Li Xunhuan: "Can you even make a profit at that price?"

"My apologies, that's a trade secret," Li Xunhuan said with a smile.

Shi Xiang was incredibly frustrated. He had taken a train all the way from Shencheng and met with Chen Guiliang before even checking into his hotel.

Only to have some interloper show up halfway through.

This deal was impossible to negotiate. Li Xunhuan was here to flip the table.

And not just his table, but the table of the entire book publishing industry!

Forcibly suppressing his anger, Shi Xiang tried his best to maintain his composure and shook hands with Chen Guiliang. "I hope we can cooperate next time."

Chen Guiliang also showed him due respect. "I can feel your sincerity, Editor Shi. I will definitely cooperate with your publishing house if I have the chance."

"Goodbye."

"Take care."

Li Xunhuan watched Shi Xiang leave the coffee shop and stirred his coffee, saying, "They're old, they're already outdated. The system of traditional publishing houses is rigid and completely unable to adapt to this era. We're all young people, the world belongs to us."

"You have that much faith in 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty'?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Xunhuan said, "It has no barrier to entry for readers. Aside from young children, its audience covers all age groups. And it's witty and humorous, close to the common person, making it very suitable for online and real-world community circulation. What's even rarer is that this happens to be a history book. Its image is positive. Parents won't treat it as a useless extracurricular book. It can even bring prestige to the reader. Having read this book, talking about it makes you seem respectable and classy."

Chen Guiliang was genuinely impressed. "Amazing, that's a very insightful analysis."

"How many words do you plan for the entire book? And what's your writing speed?" Li Xunhuan asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "The entire book will be over a million words. I can write anywhere from 30,000 to 100,000 words a month. How much I write depends on how much time I have."

"That's enough," Li Xunhuan said. "One volume per 150,000 words. Once we have enough for three volumes, we'll officially publish. 'Sprout' is a very good platform, but I hope you'll shift to the internet later, serializing on Rongshu Xia and Tianya Forum simultaneously. Once you've accumulated enough popularity, we'll take advantage of the momentum and publish the first three volumes."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Looks like I'll have to speed up. What's the deal with the tiered royalty?"

Li Xunhuan said, "Below 500,000 copies, the royalty is 15%. For every additional 100,000 copies sold, it increases by 1%, all the way up to 20%."

"President Lu, you have guts!" Chen Guiliang praised.

Li Xunhuan said, "I'll bring the contract over tomorrow. If you're worried, you can ask a senior from the law department to help you look it over."

"Can I get an advance of one hundred thousand yuan?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Xunhuan found it amusing. "Are you that short on money?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I've started two companies, and both are in their initial stages."

"Starting companies as a freshman, and two at once?" Li Xunhuan was quite surprised.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Can I get the advance?"

"Yes, I'll give it to you when we sign the contract tomorrow." Li Xunhuan wasn't short on cash after cashing out his shares. Right now, he was only short a bestselling book.

He was like a man with a hammer, searching the world for a nail!

Chen Guiliang asked, "Does President Lu live here in Beijing?"

Li Xunhuan shook his head. "I used to live in Beijing, then I ran off to Shanghai. My company is currently in Hangzhou. I came to Beijing to discuss a collaboration, but that person's novel is destined not to sell well. Yours is different. I knew it would be a huge seller after reading just two or three thousand words. Of course, the subsequent content has to maintain the quality of the opening."

"Pleasure working with you."

"Pleasure working with you."

Li Xunhuan took a sip of coffee and stood up. "Want to go for a drink together? I'm meeting Ning Caishen and Xing Yusen tonight, it's a good chance to introduce you to them."

"Next time. I have a class tonight," Chen Guiliang said truthfully.

He could meet those two anytime, but he couldn't just skip class.

Chen Guiliang pedaled his bicycle straight toward the academic building, and Li Xunhuan also hailed a taxi and sped off.
